steps: First short impact: initial P=1×6=+6; joined mass 3 kg; V_1=+2 m/s.
Slide: a=−μg=−2 m/s², so in 0.50 s v_before_2=2−2×0.50=+1 m/s.
Sliding friction magnitude is μMg=0.2×3×10=6 N, so J_f=−6×0.50=−3 N·s.
Second impact incoming P=3×1=+3; joined mass 4 kg; V_final=+3/4=+0.75 m/s.
Cross-check: first impact converts 12 J, slide removes 4.5 J, second impact converts 0.375 J. Never pool these as one collision loss.
hints: Clarify: two brief impacts surround one longer interval with external friction.
Correlate: preserve signed momentum separately in each short contact; update speed using −μg between them.
Open the way: first common speed is +2 m/s; after the slide, 3 kg enters the second collision at +1 m/s.

diagnostics.firstV: The first sticking event combines both masses; do not use the 1 kg mass alone.
diagnostics.beforeThirdV: Friction acts between contacts. Compute the speed at the END of the slide.
diagnostics.frictionJ: Include the negative sign, entire 3 kg mass and the 0.50 s sliding duration.
diagnostics.finalV: Use the second pre-contact speed +1 m/s, not the first post-contact +2 m/s.

boundarySteps: With μ=0.4 and g=10, deceleration magnitude is 4 m/s².
Stopping distance from +2 m/s is s=2²/(2×4)=0.5 m.
The stationary cart lies 0.75 m away, farther than stopping distance.
There is NO second collision: a formal contact velocity at that obstacle would be fictitious.
